subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A 'hue' refers to which property of colour?
options: The pure colour itself, such as red or blue
questions.explain: Hue is the name of the pure colour, such as red, yellow or blue, before tints or shades are added.

questions.q: What is the secondary colour made by mixing red and yellow?
questions.explain: Red mixed with yellow produces the secondary colour orange.

questions.q: Which artist is most associated with Pop Art and images of soup cans?
questions.explain: Andy Warhol was a leading Pop Art figure, famous for his Campbell's soup can images.

questions.q: Two-point perspective uses how many vanishing points?
questions.explain: Two-point perspective uses two vanishing points on the horizon, typically for objects seen at a corner.

questions.q: In a composition, what is the 'focal point'?
options: The main area that draws the viewer's eye
The darkest area of the picture
questions.explain: The focal point is the part of the composition that attracts the viewer's attention first.

questions.q: Which group are considered warm colours?
questions.explain: Reds, oranges and yellows are warm colours, while blues, greens and violets are cool.

questions.q: What is the purpose of 'annotation' in a sketchbook?
options: To explain your thinking, choices and development in words
To fill empty space with decoration
To list the cost of materials
questions.explain: Annotation uses written notes to explain your ideas, decisions and how your work is developing.

questions.q: The rule of thirds suggests you place key features where?
options: Around the edges of the frame
In the exact centre of the image
Along lines that divide the image into thirds or at their intersections
questions.explain: The rule of thirds divides the picture into a 3x3 grid and places focal points on the lines or intersections.

questions.q: In a landscape, objects placed at the bottom of the picture usually appear to be in the...
questions.explain: Objects lower in the picture plane normally read as nearer to the viewer, in the foreground.

Be unrelated to your earlier work
questions.explain: A personal response resolves your investigations and development into your own meaningful final outcome.

questions.q: What is the key difference between shape and form?
options: Shape is large, form is small
Shape is two-dimensional, form is three-dimensional
Shape is coloured, form is not
questions.explain: A shape is flat and two-dimensional, while a form has depth and appears three-dimensional.

questions.q: Which artist is closely linked to Impressionism?
questions.explain: Claude Monet was a founder of Impressionism, famous for paintings such as his water lilies.
